1 صَئِكَ , aor.
صَاَ^َ , (AZ, S, O, K,) inf. n. صَأَكٌ, (AZ, S, O,) He (a man, AZ, S, O) sweated so that there arose from him a fetid odour, (AZ, S, O, K,) from ذَفَر [app. as meaning stench of the arm-pit], or otherwise. (AZ, S, O.) ―
-b2- And, said of blood, It congealed. (O, K.) ―
-b3- And صَئِكَ بِهِ It (a thing, TA) stuck, or clave, to him. (K, TA.) Hence, accord. to the 'Eyn, صَاكَ, used in this sense in a verse of El-Aashà: (TA:) or this belongs to art. صيك, (S and O in that art.,) agreeably with the opinion of ISd. (TA in that art.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
